The concept of UBI is simple: every individual receives a regular, unconditional sum of money from the government to cover their basic needs. Similarly, Alaska's Permanent Fund Dividend, which distributes a portion of the state's oil revenues to residents, has demonstrated that UBI can be an effective poverty reduction tool.

Implementing UBI globally would provide a safety net for the most vulnerable populations, enabling them to pursue meaningful work, rather than just any job. It would also help mitigate the effects of automation, which is increasingly displacing workers worldwide. According to a McKinsey report, up to 800 million jobs could be lost worldwide due to automation by 2030. UBI would provide a necessary cushion for workers to adapt to this new reality.

Furthermore, UBI would simplify welfare systems, reduce bureaucracy, and promote economic freedom. It would also stimulate local economies, as people would have more disposable income to spend on goods and services.

The benefits of UBI are clear. It's time for us to rethink our economic systems and prioritize human well-being. I urge you to consider the merits of implementing a universal basic income globally, and I look forward to addressing any concerns you may have. Thank you.
